newsitem.title: UK: Palestinian bombers given 20 year jail terms.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian bombers given 20 year jail terms.

text.p: Two Palestinians were sentenced to 20 years in jail on Monday for plotting a bombing campaign against Jewish targets in London.

The judge at London's Old Bailey court also told Jawad Botmeh and Samar Alami that he recommend they be deported after serving their sentences. The man and woman were found guilty last week of bombings in central London in 1994 including an attack on the Israeli embassy.
The judge last week released a third man, Mahmoud Abu-Wardeh, clearing him of all charges after a two-month trial.

The three were accused of conspiring to plant two bombs -- one outside the Israeli Embassy and one near a Jewish charity in north London, causing millions of pounds (dollars) worth of damage in what prosecutors said was an attempt to sabotage the Middle East peace process. No-one was killed or seriously injured.
The three defendants had all denied the charges. The prosecution had alleged that Botmeh, 28, and his female partner Alami, 30, hoped to damage the Middle East peace process.
Israel's ambassador to Britain, Moshe Raviv, on Monday welcomed the sentence, saying he was satisfied that justice had been done.
